title: Check a 451-factor BIT schedule and its finite P104 consumer
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

A uniform 11^451 paid cutoff yields ordinary BIT cap 0.00387992804354799998 and a 6.44% smaller BIT log₂ N parameter. The pinned rational consumer and 58 outer checks yield candidate conditional κ ≥ 0.00387992804346. The 36-call BIT and 48-call rational signed profiles are unchanged. The candidate is 0.000000000002695 below the unchanged directed BIT upper 0.003879928046155.

## Task and overlap

Scoped #7852 follow-up at `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212` on main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15` uses 480 mixed-cutoff factors. #7831 and #7835 tested different cutoff schedules. #7846 at `343f7b1817e26ad3f89d2ddad313b12741d53602` has source-specific six-stage physical/precision evidence. The 451 variant retains the native, erasure, compiler, precision/tape and analytic premises, including the fresh fibre, seven-stage stock and nested seed transfer.

## Validation

The sanitized offline archive and clean CPython 3.12 replay are documented in the package. The separate compiler/audit repeat took 82.39 s and reproduced application and audit bytes. Both native orientations, separately recounted paid/target bills, 54 strict and 4 functional outer checks, the corrupted invoice and below-effective BIT cap controls pass as documented. No prime or tensor was materialized. The BIT-carrier comparison does not establish an end-to-end resource reduction.

## Credit

Credit the #7830, #7831, #7835, #7846 and inherited rational/BIT framework contributors. Separate Codex workers independently repeated the consumer replay and repricing. Clear1nsight prepared this package with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.

## Open next questions

Rebuild the 451-specific physical stock and precision interfaces, and identify an actual signed BIT improvement against the live crossing.
